title: Troubleshooting
text:
Symptom
Next step




GitHub installation fails
Read the first failing dependency in the R output. Check internet/repository access and retry after fixing it.


A compiled package fails to install
Check Rtools on Windows or the compiler/system libraries reported on Linux/macOS. See installation.


A function in this guide is missing
Check packageVersion("datapond") and find.package("datapond"). Restart R after updating. Your branch may predate the feature.


App opens but save controls are unavailable
Sign in with editor or administrator access to the intended pond; inspect any review/lifecycle lock message. Connected-pond rows are read-only.


Last pond cannot be opened
Reconnect its storage and choose Retry opening pond, or open another existing pond in the recovery dialog.


Browser tab closes but R remains busy
Stop the app in R or use Exit DataPond where offered.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Documents and templates
Run datapond::check_document_tools() and read the failed checks. Quarto, XeLaTeX and Python are separate programs. After installation or PATH changes, restart R before testing again. A successful executable check alone does not prove a document renders.
If PDF rendering reports missing TeX packages/fonts, run setup while online for a Quarto-managed TinyTeX installation. For system TeX, ask its administrator to install the reported dependencies. If a dataset-specific QMD fails but the checker passes, inspect that QMD’s paths, execution settings and analysis dependencies.
If template creation refuses a filename, choose a different project short name or review the existing document. The app deliberately does not replace it. Keep a QMD and its generated theme folder together when transferring the dataset.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Freeze, restore and review







Symptom
Next step




Prepared metadata is stale or changed
Save metadata, prepare the PDF again, open it and repeat the preview.


Freeze preview includes unexpected files
Review the dataset root, including hidden files and old bundles. Remove unwanted files deliberately, then preview again.


Release version already exists
Keep it intact and save a new version for the new release.


Restore reports changed shared references
Ask the curator to resolve the listed people/organisation/licence/vocabulary differences.


Lifecycle operation was interrupted
Use the recovery control. Keep journals, locks and staging evidence available for diagnosis.


Metadata return is stale
Inspect the differences, resolve competing edits, cancel with a reason and issue a new request.


A review return has unexpected inventory differences
Check whether the reviewer scanned the metadata-only workspace or edited out-of-scope records.

title: Troubleshooting
section: Ask for help with useful evidence
text:
Ask for help with useful evidence
Record the action, exact error, package version, operating system and whether the problem affects a practice pond or an operational pond. For document problems, include the check output. Review logs before sharing them because paths and metadata can contain sensitive information.
packageVersion("datapond")
find.package("datapond")
sessionInfo()
Do not send a full pond database or dataset just to report an installation error. A small reproducible practice example is usually more useful.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
text:
A frozen release preserves a verified set of dataset files and saved metadata under arc/. Continuing work or restoring an older draft does not overwrite that release. Use Dataset lifecycle → Frozen releases.
The current controls implement local freezing, restoration, checkpoints and recovery. They do not yet implement release publication/withdrawal, a remote published-current pointer or a QGIS plugin. Flow catalogue publication is a separate workflow.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
text:
Prepare the dataset for freezing
Save a meaningful version in major.minor.patch form (for example 1.0.0) and a citation. Finish or cancel an active metadata review. Prepare metadata.pdf through Dataset status → Human-readable metadata → Save PDF to dataset folder & download. Open the PDF, inspect the complete dataset folder, and check what an external recipient will receive.

Before freezing a version
Metadata, version and citation are saved.
Methods, inputs, outputs and quality limitations are documented.
I regenerated and opened the current metadata PDF.
The folder contains the intended files and no unwanted temporary material.
The intended distribution complies with the recorded rights and approvals.
External editors and QGIS are closed for this operation.

These personal ticks do not replace the confirmation or validation in the app. Freezing includes every file under the dataset root, including hidden files and old transport ZIPs. Remove unwanted material deliberately before previewing; the app does not guess what to exclude. Leave enough free space for staging, the archive and any preserved draft.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
text:
Freeze and verify






flowchart TD
  accTitle: Prepare, preview and freeze a version
  accDescr: Save metadata, version and citation, finish or cancel any review, then prepare and inspect the PDF and folder. Preview the saved dataset. Resolve failed checks and repeat preparation when needed. When checks pass, confirm the review and add release notes. Freeze while keeping the working copy, or freeze and close development. Select and verify the resulting release.
  save["Save metadata, version and citation;<br/>finish or cancel any active review"] --> prepare["Prepare and inspect PDF and folder"]
  prepare --> preview["Preview saved dataset"]
  preview --> checks{"Preview checks pass?"}
  checks -->|No| fix["Resolve reported issues"]
  fix --> prepare
  checks -->|Yes| confirm["Confirm PDF and folder review;<br/>enter release notes"]
  confirm --> keep["Freeze version;<br/>keep working copy"]
  confirm --> close["Freeze version and<br/>close development"]
  keep --> verify["Select and verify the new release"]
  close --> verify


 Both freeze choices preserve a verified release; they differ in what happens to the working folder. 





Choose Preview saved dataset. Review the file list and checks. Unsafe paths, symbolic links, case-colliding names or stale/changed prepared documents stop the operation.
Confirm in the app that you opened the PDF and reviewed the previewed folder, and enter release notes.
Choose Freeze version; keep working copy to continue developing, or Freeze version and close development to retire the working folder after verification.
Select the new release and verify it. A frozen version cannot be overwritten; save a different version before making the next release.

Choose an ISO validation policy only when that release requires an ISO package. A requested ISO export failure stops the freeze. For an already frozen matching draft, Close development using selected release avoids making another release and checks that its metadata and files still match.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
text:
Distribute the release
arc/releases/<release-id>/
  dataset.zip
  release.json
  files.json
  checksums.sha256
Keep the three sidecars with the ZIP when distributing outside DataPond. The app’s ZIP download currently downloads the ZIP alone; collect the sidecars from the release folder as well.
The ZIP preserves the dataset in dataset/, plus public metadata, metadata.pdf, its QMD source and portable theme, citation.txt, README.txt and a licence summary. Root QMD/Rmd development documents are acknowledged and preserved without execution. Read the recorded rights before sending the files: a successful freeze is not a distribution approval.
Private metadata snapshots remain inside .metadata_pond/. Back them up with the catalogue and archive; the public ZIP alone is not all the state needed for in-app restoration. Checksums detect changed files but do not prevent someone modifying them outside the app.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
section: Restore an older release or roll back a draft
text:
Restore an older release or roll back a draft
Restore selected release as draft restores its saved files and metadata into a new dev/ folder. The dataset UUID and catalogue ID stay the same, and the frozen release remains unchanged. If a working draft exists, the app first preserves it as a verified private checkpoint.
Roll back to selected working-draft checkpoint restores that prior draft and checkpoints the draft it replaces. Check the restored state, make your changes, then save a new version before freezing again. Releases and checkpoints do not expire automatically in this version.






flowchart TD
  accTitle: Restore a frozen release as a working draft
  accDescr: Select a frozen release and request restoration as a draft. If checks pass and a working draft exists, preserve it as a verified private checkpoint first. Restore the release files and metadata to a new development folder, inspect the restored draft, and save a new version before freezing again. The original frozen release and dataset UUID remain unchanged.
  select["Select a frozen release;<br/>Restore selected release as draft"] --> checks{"Restore checks pass?"}
  checks -->|No| resolve["Resolve reported differences<br/>with the curator, then retry"]
  resolve --> select
  checks -->|Yes| existing{"Working draft exists?"}
  existing -->|Yes| checkpoint["Preserve it as a verified<br/>private checkpoint"]
  existing -->|No| restore["Restore files and metadata<br/>into a new dev/ folder"]
  checkpoint --> restore
  restore --> inspect["Check and edit the restored draft;<br/>save a new version before freezing"]


 Restore changes the working draft while preserving the selected frozen release and the dataset’s identity. 




Restoration can stop when shared people, organisation, licence or vocabulary references have changed. Resolve the reported differences with the curator; do not overwrite shared definitions merely to force the restore.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
text:
Recover an interrupted operation
Use Recover interrupted lifecycle operation after an interruption. The app checks its operation journal and preserved files before completing or reconciling the operation. It refuses to interrupt a live process or a lock from another computer. Do not delete locks or staging folders to bypass a refusal; retain the error and ask the maintainer to inspect it.

title: Freeze, restore and use releases
text:
Use one extracted consumer cache
The current R helper can cache a release from a local pond. It stages the ZIP, verifies it, extracts and verifies the files, then exposes a stable folder named for that release. The transport ZIP is removed by default; keep_zip = TRUE deliberately retains it.
# Replace these values with an existing local pond, release ID and cache folder.
pond <- "/path/to/pond"
release_id <- "existing-release-id"
cache_root <- "/path/to/consumer-cache"
cached <- datapond::cache_dataset_release(release_id, pond, cache = cache_root)
datapond::verify_cached_dataset_release(cached)
file.path(cached, "release", "dataset", "data")
Open the required files under that last path in QGIS manually. Treat cached files as read-only, and copy them to a working dataset before editing. Keeping each release at its own path lets a project refer to a particular version. Remote Flow downloads, automatic cache eviction/project pinning and the QGIS plugin are future work.

title: Edit and maintain this guide
text:
The maintained sources live in the package repository’s guide/ folder. Open a chapter’s _content/*.qmd file in RStudio and select Visual for a document-like editing experience, or edit its source in any text editor. These shared chapter files supply both the website and offline edition.







Location
Purpose




guide/_content/
Chapter text shared by both editions


guide/*.qmd
Chapter titles, navigation and the combined offline edition


guide/_quarto.yml
Website structure and rendering options


guide/assets/
Theme, styling, logo and checklist/search behaviour


scripts/build_user_guide.R
Render and copy the built guide into the package


inst/guide/
Generated HTML shipped with DataPond; edit the sources instead



The rendered guide is interactive for readers, but browser edits do not save back into the QMD source. Use Quarto’s editor/preview workflow to maintain the text. It does not require a Shiny runtime.

title: Edit and maintain this guide
text:
Preview while writing
From a terminal at the repository root:
quarto preview guide
Quarto serves the guide locally and refreshes the preview as you save. Native website search works when served by preview or the app. For a file you open directly from disk, use offline.html, which embeds its assets and searches its own chapter text.
See Quarto’s official website guide, search documentation and HTML options for configuration details. The preview server does not publish the site to the internet.

title: Edit and maintain this guide
section: Rebuild the copy included in the package
text:
Rebuild the copy included in the package
From the repository root, run in a terminal:
Rscript scripts/build_user_guide.R
The script reads the package version, renders both editions and copies the completed site into inst/guide/. It requires Quarto at build time; colleagues reading the installed guide do not need it. Keep both source edits and generated output in the same release so GitHub installations include the guide without rendering it on the user’s computer.
After rebuilding, review navigation, search, mobile layout, links and checklists; check the standalone edition with its file copied elsewhere. Reinstall the package to see the updated bundled guide in a fresh app session.

title: Edit and maintain this guide
text:
Open the installed guide
Use the ? button beside the configuration gear, or run:
datapond::open_user_guide()
The R helper opens the self-contained offline edition. open_user_guide(browse = FALSE) returns its local path so you can copy it to a colleague. The app link serves the searchable chapter website locally while the app is running.

title: Edit and maintain this guide
text:
Keep process guidance current
When a workflow changes, update the relevant chapter alongside the code. Check instructions against a practice pond, use the exact app labels, and distinguish implemented features from planned ones. Record factual limitations such as metadata-only review scope and the current local release cache.
Process diagrams use native Quarto {mermaid} blocks in the shared chapter sources. Edit their labels and branches alongside the surrounding instructions. Keep each diagram focused on one task, include a caption plus Mermaid accTitle and accDescr text, and retain the written steps for readers who prefer them. See the Quarto diagram documentation and Mermaid accessibility guidance. After rebuilding, check that every diagram renders in both the chapter website and a separately copied offline.html, including on a narrow screen.
This repository is the source of truth. A hosted documentation site can later use the same Quarto output without maintaining a second wiki. Hosting and automatic publication have not been configured here.

title: Install DataPond
text:
Use a computer where you can install R packages and write to your chosen pond folder. Installation needs internet access to download software and dependencies; everyday metadata work and this guide can run offline.
Install R 4.1 or newer from CRAN. An editor such as RStudio Desktop is optional but convenient. Paste the R examples below into the R Console, not a system terminal.

WindowsmacOSLinux


Install R first, then RStudio if desired. If an R dependency needs compilation from source, install the Rtools version matching your R version. A managed work computer may need IT assistance. Restart R after changing system tools.


Choose the CRAN R installer for Apple Silicon or Intel as appropriate. Binary packages avoid many compilation requirements. Source builds can require additional compiler and spatial libraries; follow the error for the failing dependency.


Install R using your distribution’s supported route. Spatial dependencies can require GDAL, GEOS, PROJ and udunits2 development libraries. Ask IT to install the appropriate distribution packages; see the official sf installation notes. pak reports system dependencies where supported.

title: Install DataPond
text:
Install the package from GitHub
For the stable colleague-facing build:
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ekznw/datapond")
packageVersion("datapond")
This installs the R dependencies, including ekznwr from GitHub. It does not install Quarto, Python or a PDF engine simply because they are listed as system requirements. Follow Document tools when you need document generation or releases.


Alternative installer and development builds

If your team uses remotes:
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ekznw/datapond", dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = "never")
For features that your maintainer has made available on the development branch:
pak::pak("ekznw/datapond@develop")
Confirm the intended branch with the maintainer when following a development guide. Local changes are not available to colleagues until pushed and released. If GitHub access fails, check the repository address and your organisation’s access arrangements.

title: Install DataPond
text:
Launch and check
datapond::run_data_pond()
The app opens in a browser and R stays busy serving it. Continue with Your first pond. Use Exit DataPond where offered, or stop the running app in R, when finished. Closing only the browser tab may leave R running the app.

Ready for your first session
R is installed and opens.
DataPond installed without an error.
The app opens in my browser.

title: Install DataPond
text:
Updating an existing installation
Back up the whole pond before a package upgrade. Stop the app, restart R, run the same installation command, then start DataPond again. Check the version and use its bundled guide. Keep an untouched backup when testing a development build; reinstalling an older package is not a pond rollback procedure.

title: Your first pond
text:
Open Configuration with the gear button. Under Pond management → Open or create a data pond, choose:

Open existing pond for a folder that already contains a DataPond catalogue. You can also enter its path under Open an existing pond by path.
Create new pond for a new workspace. Choose its parent location and a new folder name, check the destination, then choose Create and open pond.

Create a practice pond first if you are learning. Creating a pond does not copy datasets from another pond. For an unavailable existing drive, reconnect it and choose Retry opening pond; do not create a replacement pond at the missing mount location.

title: Your first pond
text:
Open Configuration with the gear button. Under Pond management → Open or create a data pond, choose:

Open existing pond for a folder that already contains a DataPond catalogue. You can also enter its path under Open an existing pond by path.
Create new pond for a new workspace. Choose its parent location and a new folder name, check the destination, then choose Create and open pond.

title: Your first pond
text:
Sign in or request access
The workspace requires a local account for this pond. Choose Request access if you do not have one. An administrator verifies the request, chooses a role, and gives you a single-use activation code. Use Activate / recover access to set a passphrase of at least 15 characters, then sign in.
For the first administrator, stop the app and run this once in the local R console:
code <- datapond::setup_pond_access(
  "/path/to/your/pond", "your.username",
  first_name = "Your", last_name = "Name"
)
code
Keep the code private. It expires after 24 hours. To link an existing metadata person, use their verified person_id instead of supplying a new name. Existing seeded names do not automatically grant access.
Viewers browse metadata. Editors can edit and use dataset workflows. Pond administrators also approve accounts, manage shared reference data, and use Flow. Administrators open Configuration → Manage accounts to approve requests, change roles, disable accounts or issue recovery codes. File downloads require editor or administrator access. Sign out through Configuration when finished.
If the administrator is locked out, the installation owner can run datapond::recover_pond_access("/path/to/your/pond", "your.username") in the trusted local R console. Application login does not prevent someone with direct filesystem or R-console access from changing the underlying data.
For administrator procedures, SharePoint caches and future server hosting, see Manage accounts and deployment. Local accounts are separate on each workstation; they do not synchronise through SharePoint.

title: Your first pond
text:
Understand the folders
my_pond/
  metadata.db       Local catalogue
  src/              Supplied or reference datasets
  dev/              Datasets being developed
  arc/              Archived material and frozen releases
  .metadata_pond/    Internal settings, snapshots and recovery records
A working dataset normally has data/, docs/ and scripts/ subfolders. Keep the data development report at the dataset root if that is your project convention. DataPond can acknowledge root QMD/Rmd documents when preparing metadata and releases.
Avoid manually moving a managed dataset folder or renaming its catalogue database. Use the app’s lifecycle/transfer controls so folder location and catalogue records stay consistent.

title: Your first pond
section: Open a connected pond for editing
text:
Open a connected pond for editing
Configuration can connect additional existing ponds with recognisable names. Access to their records requires signing in to the relevant pond. ★ Current identifies the active pond, and Show current pond datasets only narrows the list.
Open the required pond from Configuration or the sign-in screen, sign in there, then select its dataset to edit. Login rights are checked separately for every pond. An unavailable connected pond is omitted from results until reconnected and refreshed; its connection is retained.

title: Your first pond
text:
Back up the whole pond
Close the app and external writers before taking a filesystem backup. Preserve metadata.db, dataset folders, arc/ and the hidden .metadata_pond/ directory together. A frozen public ZIP is useful for distribution, but does not contain all private restoration or review state. Test your organisation’s restore procedure on a copy.
Account security is stored separately under the installation’s DataPond configuration directory (security/). Back it up privately as well. Dataset bundles do not carry passwords or login rights; moving a pond or using another installation requires local account setup.

title: Describe a dataset
text:
Open the intended pond and sign in with editor or administrator access.
Choose Start a new dataset. Select Create new folders in beside Create folder & save in the Dataset guide: dev/ for development or src/ for received/reference data. The same selection is available under Configuration (gear) → Lifecycle folder status; both controls share the active pond’s default. Existing datasets stay in their saved locations.
Select the metadata entry profile in Configuration. Essential — Prickly Porcupine keeps the initial form smaller. Full — Armoured Pangolin exposes more detail. Show additional metadata fields lets you add detail as needed; switching profiles preserves entered values.
Enter the title, publication date, version, abstract, theme keyword and a dataset organisation with a usable code. Version is required in both profiles and starts at 0.1.0 for a new working draft; use 1.0.0 for the first release. The Full profile also requires purpose and applicable topic information. Follow the save validation messages for your record.
Choose Save dataset and check its saved folder and citation. Dataset naming uses the saved descriptive fields; the dataset UUID provides its stable identity.

Do not invent an unknown publication date to satisfy a form. Resolve it with the dataset custodian before saving. A draft passing its save checks does not mean that all release or ISO metadata requirements are complete.
Field labels use * for an entry required for the stated action or completion, and ◇ for an entry required under the condition described below its label. Unmarked entries are optional, but supplied values must still be valid. For example, an embargo end date is required when embargo is Yes; a permission reference is needed to complete an assessment based on external permission. Requirements for a complete assessment or ISO export do not by themselves block a draft save.
Existing versions are preserved when editing. Change the version deliberately when appropriate; changing it does not release or archive the dataset. Lifecycle status is managed separately.

title: Describe a dataset
section: Put data and supporting material in the right place
text:
Put data and supporting material in the right place
Put the actual dataset payload in data/. Put supporting reports and scripts at the dataset root or in docs/ and scripts/, as appropriate. Keep portable relative paths in your reports and scripts.
Use the data-file scan to inspect the files. Review the results, then choose Save live scan to database to update the saved inventory. A preview alone does not update it. Scanning a custom folder is an inspection action; check that you are saving the managed dataset’s scan.
Spatial file inspection can derive useful information, but review the results before relying on them. A map preview does not establish accuracy, licensing or fitness for a particular use.
To profile attributes, open Configuration → Attribute profiling, select Enable attribute profiling, and click Save profiling setting. This setting is saved for the active pond and requires editor or administrator access. Under Data files, select a saved file, check Include in attribute profiling in File review, and click Save file review. Then use Profile selected file attributes / raster layers under Attribute profile / data dictionary. Enabling the setting does not start profiling automatically; disabling it preserves existing profiles.

title: Describe a dataset
section: Describe what another user needs to know
text:
Describe what another user needs to know







Metadata
Practical question to answer




Title, abstract and purpose
What is this dataset, and what was it created for?


Version and dates
Which revision is this, when was it published, and what period does it describe?


Authors, organisation and contact
Who created it and whom should a recipient contact?


Keywords and geographic/temporal coverage
How can someone find it and assess its coverage?


Spatial reference, resolution and attributes
How should users interpret coordinates, units, fields and codes?


Lineage and quality
How was it made, what was checked, and what limitations remain?


Licensing, access and distribution
Who may obtain it, use it and redistribute it, and under which conditions?


Citation and supporting documents
How should it be cited, and where are the methods and evidence?



Save edits before generating reports, validating exports or freezing a version. Use Dataset status to inspect outstanding metadata work. Add the detailed methods through Lineage and development reports.

title: Describe a dataset
section: Use a shared organisation email as the contact
text:
Use a shared organisation email as the contact
A generic or shared mailbox, such as data.requests@example.org, belongs in the organisation’s Contact email field. Do not create a fictitious person called “Data Requests” to hold the address.

Under Organisations → Add / edit organisation, select the organisation, enter its Contact email, and choose Update selected organisation. For a new record, complete the required organisation fields and choose Add as new organisation.
In Dataset Intro → Owning Organisation(s), select the organisation, choose its appropriate role and click Add if it is not already listed. The point-of-contact organisation choices come from this list.
Under Point of Contact, leave Select Contact Person set to No individual contact, select the Point of contact organisation, choose the appropriate Role (for example, Distributor when the organisation provides access or copies), and click Add POC.
Choose Save dataset before generating metadata or exporting it.

The shared mailbox is then associated with the organisation and included in its contact details in ISO metadata exports. A named individual can be added as a separate contact when needed. If the mailbox serves a particular department, use that department’s organisation record and its contact email.

title: Describe a dataset
text:
Check the human-readable metadata
In Dataset status → Human-readable metadata, choose Save PDF to dataset folder & download. This writes metadata.pdf and citation.txt at the dataset root and downloads the same PDF. Open it and check the identity, version, description, contacts, rights, lineage and any missing information.
Repeat PDF preparation after relevant metadata or document changes. Freezing verifies and preserves the prepared PDF; it does not silently refresh it. Software and package details belong in the development report, so the release README can point readers there.

title: Describe a dataset
text:
Understand ISO metadata and validation
DataPond can turn the saved dataset description into standardised, machine-readable metadata for exchange with catalogues and other information systems. The export draws on related geographic-information standards:

ISO 19115-1 defines the metadata used to describe a resource, including its identity, citation, contacts, extent, constraints, distribution and lineage.
ISO 19115-3 provides the XML implementation used by DataPond to encode that metadata in a form software can exchange and validate.
ISO 19110 defines a feature catalogue. When applicable, DataPond generates a linked catalogue describing the fields or attributes in vector and tabular data.
ISO 19157 defines data-quality information. Structured quality measures and results recorded in DataPond can therefore be carried into the metadata package.

The purpose of generation is interoperability: a recipient should receive consistently structured metadata that software can inspect as well as people can read. Validation checks that the generated XML and any linked feature catalogue follow the bundled schemas and rules. It also checks registered codes, dates, extents, references, relevant semantic consistency, cited local files and package integrity. The validated package contains the metadata XML, any generated feature catalogue, its validation report and cited local supporting documents or scripts. It does not contain the dataset payload.
The Essential — Prickly Porcupine and Full — Armoured Pangolin profiles control metadata entry and completion assessment; they are not different ISO standards or validation levels. A record prepared with either profile can produce locally validated ISO metadata. Essential can pass when the saved information is sufficient and consistent for that dataset, including any applicable detail added through Show additional metadata fields. Full prompts for richer metadata, but selecting or completing Full does not by itself guarantee ISO validity. In both profiles, the ISO validation result is the evidence that the saved export passed the selected local checks.
To validate an export:

Save the current dataset edits.
Open Dataset status → ISO metadata validation & export.
Choose the validation policy and select Check saved metadata.
Use the reported issues to open and correct the relevant metadata sections, save, and check again.
Download Validate & download ISO package when it becomes available. DataPond reassesses the saved record and supporting files during download.

The download remains blocked until the selected policy, export semantics and local-file checks pass. Additional validation requires Python with lxml, and ZIP download requires the zip utility. A local pass confirms conformance with DataPond’s declared validation scope; it does not verify that the entered facts are true, certify the dataset universally, or guarantee acceptance by a particular receiving catalogue.

title: Manage accounts and deployment
text:
DataPond login controls actions through the app. SharePoint permissions control access to the shared library, and operating-system permissions control local files. These are separate controls: a DataPond administrator does not automatically become a SharePoint administrator.








Scenario
Where accounts and approvals live
Who controls the files




Colleagues run DataPond locally and obtain data from SharePoint
Each operating-system user’s DataPond configuration, separately for each local pond path
SharePoint/library owners control remote access; workstation owners control downloaded copies


Colleagues use a future shared server through their browsers
The server service account’s DataPond configuration, provided all app processes use the same configuration and pond path
Server operators control storage and the service account’s permissions



The first release has no central account synchronisation across workstations. Approving a colleague on your computer does not approve them on theirs. Disabling their account in your installation does not revoke their other installations or erase downloaded data. People who own the local R process and files can use trusted R functions directly; local app roles are not an organisational security boundary against those people.

title: Manage accounts and deployment
text:
Find administrators and change access
Sign in to the relevant pond and open Configuration → Manage accounts. The Pond accounts table lists login accounts, roles and statuses. Rows with role admin are administrators; active means activated, while invited means awaiting activation. Seeded metadata people without login accounts do not appear as approved users merely because they exist in Parties.
Select an account’s row, then use the controls below it:







Task
Action




Change permissions
Choose Role, then Apply role and status


Suspend an activated account
Set Account status to Disabled, then Apply role and status


Re-enable an activated account
Set status to Active, confirm the role, then Apply role and status


Approve a new request
Choose the role and verified metadata person, then Approve pending request


Reject a request
Set status to Rejected, then Apply role and status


Replace a forgotten password or expired invitation
Select an active/invited account and choose Issue activation / recovery code


Review access events
Expand Access audit; times are UTC and actors/targets use account IDs



Changing a role or status signs the affected account out. The final active/invited administrator cannot be removed. To reopen a rejected request, return it to Pending approval and approve it after verification. An invitation disabled before activation must return to Awaiting activation, followed by a new code.







Role
Allowed work




Viewer
Browse the authenticated pond’s metadata and maps


Editor
Viewer access plus editing, scans, imports, exports, file/package downloads and dataset workflows, subject to existing ownership rules


Pond administrator
Editor access plus account management, shared parties/vocabularies, review acceptance and Flow



Roles apply to a pond, not individual datasets. Licensing and embargo fields describe policy; they do not enforce separate dataset permissions. Visible metadata can be copied. Grant access only where the person may see the pond’s metadata.
To browse another local pond from the current Pond overview, add it under Pond connections, select it, enter that pond’s username and password, and choose Sign in to selected catalogue. Leave Show current pond datasets only unchecked. Connected access is read-only and lasts for the current app session, subject to session expiry and account revocation. Sign out, switching ponds, or closing the session clears connected sign-ins. Switch to the target pond and sign in there to edit records. A pond labelled Sign-in required has not yet been authenticated; an unavailable folder must first be reconnected.
The local launcher uses http://127.0.0.1:5751 by default so its browser address remains stable. Both sign-in forms support browser password-manager autofill. Save your credentials in your browser and select the appropriate saved account for the pond; ponds share the same local website address. To use another fixed port, run datapond::run_data_pond(port = 5752) or set options(datapond.port = 5752) in your R startup configuration. If the port is occupied, stop the other app instance or choose another port. Passing port = NULL restores Shiny’s automatic port selection.

title: Manage accounts and deployment
text:
Set up and onboard people
The first administrator must be set up from the trusted R console outside a running Shiny session. For someone already in the metadata catalogue, verify their numeric person ID and use it:
code <- datapond::setup_pond_access(
  data_pond = "/path/to/your/pond",
  username = "your.username",
  person_id = 18L  # Example only: replace with the verified ID in this pond.
)
code
For a genuinely new person, replace person_id with first_name, last_name and optionally email. An existing-email error means you should verify and select the existing person, not create a duplicate. Setup refuses to replace an existing account store.
For subsequent accounts:

The colleague selects Request access in the intended installation and pond.
An administrator of that same installation and pond selects the request in Manage accounts, verifies identity, assigns a role and links the correct existing metadata person (or chooses Create a new person).
The administrator chooses Approve pending request and gives the displayed code privately to the colleague. DataPond does not send email or verify email ownership automatically.
The colleague selects Activate / recover access, enters their username and code, sets a passphrase of at least 15 characters, then signs in.

Activation and recovery codes work once and expire after 24 hours. Recovery replaces the password and revokes sessions; administrators cannot view passwords. An administrator recovering their own account must ask another administrator or use datapond::recover_pond_access("/path/to/your/pond", "your.username") in the trusted R console. Sign out when finished; sessions expire after 30 minutes without accepted activity or 12 hours overall.






flowchart TD
  accTitle: Onboard a colleague to a pond
  accDescr: After the first administrator has been set up, a colleague requests access to the intended pond. An administrator of that installation and pond verifies identity, links the metadata person, chooses a role and approves the request. The administrator privately shares a single-use code. The colleague activates access within 24 hours, sets a passphrase of at least 15 characters and signs in. An expired code requires a new code from the administrator.
  request["Colleague: Request access"] --> verify["Administrator: verify identity;<br/>link person and choose role"]
  verify --> approve["Administrator: Approve pending request"]
  approve --> code["Share single-use code privately"]
  code --> valid{"Code still valid<br/>within 24 hours?"}
  valid -->|No| reissue["Administrator: issue a new code"]
  reissue --> code
  valid -->|Yes| activate["Colleague: Activate / recover access;<br/>set passphrase of at least 15 characters"]
  activate --> signin["Colleague: sign in to this pond"]


 Account approval and activation happen within the same installation and pond. The administrator shares the code privately.

title: Manage accounts and deployment
section: Scenario 1: local use with SharePoint and caching
text:
Scenario 1: local use with SharePoint and caching
Use SharePoint as the distribution location and keep a clearly designated master pond. Colleagues can work with local metadata and fetch larger datasets when needed. SharePoint access does not sign them in to DataPond, and local DataPond approval does not grant SharePoint access.

Published catalogue and on-demand files through Flow
This workflow is implemented, but all Flow controls currently require a local pond administrator, including remote metadata browsing and downloads. Viewer/editor accounts cannot use this route. A separate restricted consumer role is future work; do not grant administrative access on the master merely to let someone cache data.
The introduction cards and tabs follow this order. Read remote pond opens first:







Tab
Use it to




1. Read remote pond
Browse a published pond, refresh cached metadata and download selected datasets. The remote pond stays read-only.


2. Run Flows
Preview and run saved flows, or publish the active pond using its saved publication settings.


3. Define connections
Connect remote libraries, save named local folders and choose transfer limits.


4. Design flow
Choose source, destination and copy/mirror options, then save a reusable flow.



The two setup tabs use muted sand colours. Complete connection and flow setup before running a new routine. Show Define connections tab hides or restores the connection tab without clearing its settings; it starts hidden when saved flows exist. Pond publication has its own settings in Run Flows and does not require a saved routine.
To publish and consume a pond:

The master custodian opens Flow → Run Flows → Publish pond and enters Publication destination. The source is the active pond. Select Also upload registered dataset folders (data, documents and scripts) if the files should accompany the catalogue. Save publication settings remembers the destination and upload choice for this pond; Preview / retry pond publication saves them too. Review the plan and log, then choose Run flow. The snapshot uses SQLite’s backup API. Treat the published catalogue as a copy of the metadata database: publish only to readers authorised to receive that metadata.
On the consumer workstation, set up a separate local working pond and its local account. Configure the authorised SharePoint connection in Flow → Define connections. Cloud credentials belong to the operating-system account running the app.
In Flow → Read remote pond, enter the configured remote pond folder and an empty Local pond cache folder. Use Connect / refresh metadata only. A SharePoint web URL is not a configured remote path.
Browse the cached catalogue offline. Select a dataset and choose Download / update selected dataset when its files are needed; fetching new content requires connectivity and remote permission.
Use Remove selected download from local pond cache to reclaim space. This removes that local download while retaining cached metadata and the remote dataset.

The remote cache is read-only in DataPond and does not upload edits. It is authorised by the cloud connection and the local Flow role, not by logging in to the publisher’s DataPond account store. For changes, use a separate working pond and the dataset transfer or metadata review workflow, then have the custodian accept and republish the result. This differs from the frozen-release cache helper, which currently reads release packages from a local pond.





flowchart TD
  accTitle: Publish a catalogue and fetch local copies through Flow
  accDescr: The master custodian previews and runs publication to an authorised SharePoint folder, optionally including registered dataset folders. Once publication completes, a consumer with a configured cloud connection and local pond administrator access refreshes metadata into a local read-only cache. If published dataset files are needed, download the selected dataset. Removing a local download retains the cached metadata and remote dataset; edits must go through a separate working pond and exchange workflow.
  master["Master custodian: preview publication;<br/>choose whether to include dataset folders"] --> run["Run flow; wait for publication to finish"]
  run --> remote["SharePoint: published catalogue<br/>and any uploaded dataset folders"]
  remote -->|Authorised cloud connection| metadata["Consumer: Connect / refresh metadata only"]
  metadata --> browse["Browse cached metadata offline"]
  browse -->|Files needed and published| download["While online: Download / update<br/>selected dataset"]
  download --> use["Use the local read-only copy"]
  use -->|Reclaim local space| remove["Remove selected download;<br/>retain metadata and remote dataset"]


 Flow publishes from the master to SharePoint; consumers refresh metadata and download files into a read-only local cache. All Flow actions require a local pond administrator. 



For ordinary file transfers, Design flow → Choose a destination location lists both Saved folders and Configured remotes. Selecting a remote fills in its library root, such as team_data:; append the destination subfolder in Flow to — destination. Whole-pond publication instead uses Run Flows → Publish pond → Publication destination, for example team_data:published/my_pond. To bookmark a full path, use Define connections → Saved locations → Save location. If a connection was added outside the app, use Browse locations and libraries → Detect configured libraries and drives in Define connections to refresh the choices.


Leave a publication running
Running or queued Flow jobs count as activity and prevent the 30-minute idle timeout while the app remains connected. Keep the app open and the computer awake. Normal idle expiry resumes when the job finishes, fails or is cancelled; waiting at a private cloud sign-in prompt does not extend the session.
Jobs are still attached to the app session. Explicit sign-out, revoked access, closing the app or reaching the absolute 12-hour session limit cancels them. Unattended jobs that survive disconnection or run beyond that limit require a separate background-job facility, which this release does not provide.
If publication is interrupted, sign in again and open Run Flows → Publish pond. The destination and dataset-upload choice are restored for the active pond. Check them, choose Preview / retry pond publication, then Run flow. Completed unchanged files can be reused; interrupted files may need transferring again. A partial upload is not a completed publication: wait for the final catalogue and manifest steps to finish before telling colleagues it is ready.


OneDrive-synced SharePoint folders
Where colleagues use OneDrive Files On-Demand instead of Flow, ensure required files are downloaded before offline work. On Windows, Always keep on this device retains files locally; Free up space makes them online-only. Deleting files in the synced folder can delete the shared copies too. These controls belong to OneDrive, not DataPond. See Microsoft’s Files On-Demand guidance.
For the working catalogue, use a local pond outside automatic sync and distribute a consistent snapshot or an exchange package. Do not have multiple workstations edit and sync copies of the same live metadata.db: file synchronisation does not merge database transactions. Copying a database while a transaction is active can produce an inconsistent copy; use the app’s publication snapshot or close all database writers before a filesystem copy. This operating recommendation follows SQLite’s guidance on backup and restore during transactions.


Removing local users’ access
The library owner removes SharePoint permissions; the relevant installation administrator disables the DataPond account. Previously downloaded metadata and data remain on the workstation. Handle retention or removal through the organisation’s device and data procedures. There is no remote cache wipe or central workstation audit in this release.

title: Manage accounts and deployment
text:
Scenario 2: future server-hosted access
Server hosting is a deployment option to prepare and validate, not a service provisioned by this release. Colleagues would open an HTTPS address; R, the catalogue, cloud connections and caches would run on the server. A browser download creates a separate client copy, while Flow’s local cache would be on the server.
Use a dedicated service account with persistent, protected local storage. Bootstrap its administrator from an R console running as that service account, using the same configuration directory and canonical pond path as the hosted app. All app processes intended to share accounts must use that same store. Separate OS users, containers with separate configuration directories, or different pond paths do not automatically share accounts.
In that arrangement, Manage accounts becomes the shared control point for browser users of that server and pond. Disabling an account revokes its sessions there, but does not affect SharePoint membership or files already downloaded elsewhere. Direct server R/filesystem access remains trusted and should be restricted to operators.
Before opening remote access, the operator must configure HTTPS, restrict service-account file/cloud permissions, preserve and back up the account store, and validate concurrent use, session routing and recovery in the chosen hosting environment. Flow administrators operate with that service account’s file and configured cloud access, not each browser user’s SharePoint identity. Do not expose personal cloud credentials through a shared server. SSO, MFA, automatic Microsoft identity-to-role mapping and distributed multi-host account storage are not implemented in this release.

title: Manage accounts and deployment
section: Backups and changes of machine or path
text:
Backups and changes of machine or path
Back up the pond and the account store separately. Locate the latter with:
file.path(tools::R_user_dir("datapond", which = "config"), "security")
That private directory contains password hashes, token records and the access audit. Keep it out of shared dataset folders and publication bundles. Take consistent backups with writers stopped, protect them, and test restoration on a copy.
Account stores are keyed by canonical pond path under that OS user’s configuration. Moving a pond, changing users or moving to another machine requires local setup or a deliberately managed restoration; copying metadata.db alone transfers neither passwords nor roles. Legacy administrative flags in the portable metadata are not login permissions. The Access audit describes that account store’s events, not all SharePoint activity or changes made by external R scripts.

title: Set up document tools
text:
Run setup once while online
Stop the app and run in R:
datapond::setup_document_tools()
The helper checks Quarto, XeLaTeX and Python, then tries the metadata PDF and the development template’s PDF, Word and HTML outputs in a temporary folder. It does not modify a dataset or execute its analysis.
If Quarto or Python is missing, setup prints installation instructions. Install Quarto and Python as needed, restart R so it sees the new programs, and rerun setup. Installing the R package named quarto is not a substitute for installing the Quarto command-line program.
When XeLaTeX is missing, setup can install Quarto-managed TinyTeX and the required theme packages. It tests an existing system TeX installation without modifying it. If that installation reports missing fonts or packages, ask its administrator to resolve them. An incomplete existing TinyTeX directory is not forcibly replaced.

title: Set up document tools
text:
Verify before going offline
result <- datapond::check_document_tools()
result$checks
result$ready
Proceed when result$ready is TRUE. This check renders test documents with software/package downloads disabled. The app offers the same action under Configuration → Document tools → Check document tools. A quick check_document_tools(verify = FALSE) only detects programs; it does not prove rendering works.






flowchart TD
  accTitle: Check document tools before going offline
  accDescr: Run setup while online and follow any installation instructions. Restart R after installing tools, then run check_document_tools. If ready is false, resolve the failed checks and check again. A true result means the document toolchain passed its test renders.
  setup["Run setup_document_tools() online"] --> install["Follow any installation instructions;<br/>restart R after installing tools"]
  install --> check["Run check_document_tools()"]
  check --> ready{"result$ready is TRUE?"}
  ready -->|No| fix["Resolve the reported failed checks"]
  fix --> check
  ready -->|Yes| offline["Document toolchain ready for offline use"]


 Complete setup and a rendering check before relying on document generation offline. 




The first online setup can take time and download a TeX distribution. It is an explicit user action, never an automatic part of starting the app. After setup, normal app PDF generation leaves automatic TeX package downloads disabled.


Custom software locations

Set DATAPOND_QUARTO (or QUARTO_PATH) to the Quarto executable and DATAPOND_RELEASE_PYTHON to the Python executable. For example, using your actual paths:
Sys.setenv(DATAPOND_QUARTO = "/path/to/quarto")
Sys.setenv(DATAPOND_RELEASE_PYTHON = "/path/to/python3")
datapond::check_document_tools()
Use .Renviron for persistent settings, then restart R. Use executable paths, not their parent folders.

title: Start here
text: Keep the data, its description and its history together. This guide takes you from installing DataPond to handing someone a documented, frozen dataset.

title: Start here
section: A practical route through the app
text:
A practical route through the app
Install → Open a pond → Sign in → Save a dataset → Add files and lineage → Review metadata → Prepare PDF → Freeze a version.





flowchart TD
  accTitle: A practical route through DataPond
  accDescr: Install DataPond, open a pond and sign in. Save a draft, add files and lineage, review metadata, then prepare and inspect the PDF. Freeze and verify a release before checking distribution approval and sharing the ZIP with its sidecars.
  setup["Install DataPond, open a pond and sign in"] --> draft["Save a dataset draft"]
  draft --> describe["Add files, metadata and lineage"]
  describe --> review["Review metadata"]
  review --> pdf["Prepare and inspect metadata PDF"]
  pdf --> freeze["Freeze and verify a version"]
  freeze --> share["Check distribution approval;<br/>share ZIP and sidecars"]


 From a working draft to a verified release. Distribution is a separate decision. 



Use a small practice pond for your first run. A saved draft, a reviewed dataset and a frozen release are different milestones. Freezing records a fixed version; your organisation still decides whether it may be distributed.

title: Start here
text:
Using this guide
Use chapter navigation and search to find a task. Code blocks have copy buttons; commands are examples for you to run, never executed by the guide. Installation tabs separate operating systems. Checklists remember your ticks where browser storage permits; they do not inspect or change a dataset and are not an approval record.
Process diagrams summarise the written instructions. On a narrow screen, scroll wider diagrams sideways; keyboard users can focus the diagram and use the arrow keys.
The Offline edition combines every chapter into one HTML file with its own search. Save that file to read or share without R, Quarto or a running app. External reference links still need an internet connection.

title: Lineage and development reports
text:
Open Dataset workspace → Lineage → Lineage authority and supporting documents → Add data development template.

Use a saved, unlocked draft in src/ or dev/, while signed in with editor or administrator access.
Choose Microsoft Word for colleagues who want to type directly into a report, or Quarto for an editable source that can render to PDF, Word and HTML.
Optionally enter a short project name such as pisr.
Choose Add template to dataset folder. The app creates data_dev_pisr.docx or data_dev_pisr.qmd at the dataset root. A Quarto copy also receives its portable data_dev_pisr_theme/ folder.

Existing files are never overwritten. The report is registered in Supporting documents, but is not automatically treated as finished lineage evidence. Adding a template needs no rendering software. An active review or lifecycle operation may prevent adding it until that operation is completed or cancelled.

title: Lineage and development reports
text:
Write the development history
The common template covers revision history, project summary, main steps, inputs, detailed processing, outputs and quality checks, conclusions and appendices. For each important step record its purpose, inputs, operation, decisions, outputs and checks. Include software versions, packages and run evidence in the report so another person can understand how the data were produced.
Instructional callouts are useful while writing. Keep them during development, then remove or resolve them before declaring the report complete. The draft PISR and PU reports are examples of work in progress, not completed instructions to copy as factual methods.







Word workflow
Quarto workflow




Open the .docx and replace prompts with your methods.
Edit the .qmd in RStudio’s visual or source editor, or another text editor.


Use its styles for headings, captions and tables.
Keep the YAML theme references and the adjacent theme folder together.


Save the report and, if needed, export PDF in your editor.
Render to the desired format with Quarto.


Record software/packages manually.
Record software/packages in the report; review any executable code before rendering.



Word and Quarto copies do not synchronise. Decide which source your team maintains. Editing a rendered Word output does not update its QMD source.

Render a Quarto report
In a terminal, change to the dataset folder and substitute your actual filename:
quarto render data_dev_pisr.qmd --to html
quarto render data_dev_pisr.qmd --to docx
quarto render data_dev_pisr.qmd --to pdf

DataPond’s metadata PDF and frozen-release operations acknowledge and preserve QMD/Rmd documents without executing their analysis.

title: Lineage and development reports

text:
Make the completed report part of lineage
Review its record under Supporting documents, then select the authoritative document in Lineage authority and supporting documents. Save a concise lineage summary in the app, with the detailed method in the report. Review any include-in-lineage choices; a newly added blank template starts unselected.
Existing root data_dev*.qmd or .Rmd documents can also support lineage. Check the registered document paths after scanning. Keep the document and its styles inside the dataset for portability. Reprepare metadata.pdf when its lineage references change, then review and freeze the complete folder.

  edit -->|Send return ZIP| inspect["Master: Inspect return"]
  inspect --> checks{"Baseline unchanged<br/>and checks pass?"}
  checks -->|Yes| accept["Pond administrator: record decision;<br/>accept reviewed metadata"]
  checks -->|No| resolve["Resolve competing work;<br/>cancel with a reason"]
  resolve -->|Fresh request| request


 Metadata review is a round trip between the master and a separate review pond. Send both ZIPs through your agreed channel.

title: Transfer and metadata review
text:
Request a metadata review
In the master pond, use Pond links / Dataset transfer → Metadata review exchange. Save the dataset and enter the responsible colleague. Include the dataset folder in the review request is selected by default: supporting documents, data, other subfolders and root files (including hidden files) travel with the metadata. Existing DataPond transfer ZIPs and temporary transfer metadata are excluded; files outside the dataset folder are not included. Clear the option for a smaller, metadata-only request. Choose Create metadata review request, download the ZIP and send it through your agreed review channel. The app does not automatically notify the reviewer or upload it.
One request can be active per dataset. Keep the master’s private .metadata_pond/reviews/ records: they contain the baseline needed to accept the return. Try to avoid changing the master or its files while a review is outstanding.

title: Transfer and metadata review
text:
Work as the reviewer
Import the request with Import dataset into a separate local pond that does not already contain the dataset UUID. Use a fresh review pond for a repeated assignment. Sign in to that pond, edit metadata, record the reason/status in Metadata review, and save. Choose Create metadata review return and send the resulting ZIP back.
If the sender included the dataset folder, supporting documents and data are available in the imported review workspace for reference. Otherwise the workspace contains metadata only: do not scan its empty data folder. Review returns contain metadata only, even when the request included files. Changes to files, file inventories, supporting-document records and shared definitions are outside this review-return workflow and will not be accepted into the master.

title: Transfer and metadata review
text:
Inspect and accept the return
In the master, select the returned ZIP and choose Inspect return. Read the comparison with the issued baseline. An active pond administrator records the acceptance decision and chooses Accept reviewed metadata into master.
Acceptance updates the existing record and UUID, preserves previous metadata and appends review history. If the master metadata or files have changed, acceptance stops. Resolve the competing work, cancel the old request with a reason and issue a fresh request; this version does not automatically merge it.
An accepted return does not publish itself. Where your team uses Flow, Flow → Publish pond is a separate catalogue publication step. It does not establish a published-current pointer for frozen releases. Follow your team’s distribution approvals before sharing data.
